title: Pollinator decline driver attribution
bottleneck: Wild pollinators are declining globally, threatening a third of crop production, but the relative roles of pesticides, habitat loss, parasites, and climate shifts remain unquantified in most regions — and the drivers interact synergistically in ways single-factor studies miss. Managed honeybees mask wild pollinator losses in agricultural statistics, and long-term monitoring exists for almost nowhere in the tropics where pollination dependence is highest. Without attribution, interventions are guesswork.
why_it_blocks: Pollination services are worth hundreds of billions annually; getting the diagnosis wrong wastes the response. If pesticides are the main driver, regulation works; if it is habitat fragmentation, landscape restoration is needed — and we largely do not know which.
current_state: The EU's pesticide restrictions and habitat schemes are large natural experiments, but rigorous driver attribution studies remain rare. Pollinator monitoring networks are expanding but still cover a small fraction of agricultural landscapes.
